scope: Source claims, explanation order, example roles, prerequisite clarity and conditions. No rendered-motion, actual-audio or final-footage approval.
result: Source thesis, five-section order and conclusion retained; targeted clarification revisions applied.

revisions.issue: The source recommendation to try stronger animation beyond an initially sufficient result was too implicit.
revisions.change: Explicitly ask the animator to increase amplitude and compare the readable force at actual gameplay size.
revisions.why: Preserve the central Too Much is Just Right lesson rather than reduce it to a neutral definition of exaggeration.

revisions.issue: Screen-scale and animation-amplitude comparisons could change two variables at once.
revisions.change: First show the same clip at large and small size; then fix the small-view camera and playback time while changing amplitude.
revisions.why: Separate observation of information loss from the controlled demonstration of the proposed remedy.

revisions.issue: Rotation versus translation and the importance of available rig controls needed prerequisites.
revisions.change: Define rotation around the joint anchor and translation of that anchor; compare fixed and movable shoulder controls.
revisions.why: Make the source shoulder limitation and broader control range understandable without claiming the same implementation for an uninspected commercial game.

revisions.issue: The illustrative 100→110→100 movement had no defined units or origin.
revisions.change: Define start 0 cm, target 100 cm, overshoot 110 cm and return 100 cm within the same overall duration.
revisions.why: The viewer can see the target and the 10 cm excess. Values are explicitly our illustrative example, not a measurement of a game.

revisions.issue: The role of the 2D spike expansion example was too implicit.
revisions.change: Describe the largest expanded spike shape followed immediately by the slightly smaller settled shape.
revisions.why: Preserve the positional-overshoot-to-2D-shape demonstration sequence and its example role.

retainedEssentialConditions: The original comparison uses different actions; our controlled same-clip comparison must not be attributed to that source comparison.
Unusual paused poses may have a deliberate role in the full motion; fix actual joint or surface errors without deleting the intended motion role.
Early constrained-rig history is not generalized to every old game or current commercial implementation.
The final amount of exaggeration must be judged at actual camera size and native playback speed.
